fields.claim_quote:
By the definition of [[Definition:Content of Rational Polynomial|content]], and using that $a \in \Z$:
:$\cont {b n q f} = a \cont {n f}$
fields.explanation:
The challenged integral-scalar content step permits negative integera; normalization of content is nonnegative. Keep a=-1,b=n=2,q=-1/2,f=X+1, henceg=nf=2X+2 andbnqf=-g. Both contents are2, whilea*contentg=-2. Actual integer Polynomial.content; monicity establishescontent(X+1)=1, and content_C_mul computescontentg andcontent(-g).

Content is defined as a gcd of coefficients (nonnegative by the standard gcd convention) and, for nonzero rational polynomials, as the positive rational c with f = c f* and f* primitive; the zero polynomial has content 0. Hence cont(a g) >= 0 always, while a cont(g) < 0 whenever a < 0 and g != 0, so the two sides cannot be equal for any negative scalar. The proof never splits on the sign of a (or b), and the omission propagates verbatim to the last line. The correct identities are cont(a g) = |a| cont(g) and cont(q f) = |q| cont(f).
fields.flaw: The proof asserts that for an integer a, cont(b n q f) = a * cont(n f), i.e. that pulling an integer scalar a out of the content multiplies the content by a itself. For nonzero nf, this displayed integral-scalar step is false when a is negative, because normalized content is nonnegative; the correct identity is cont(a g)=|a| cont(g). The proof never splits on the sign of a or b, and the same omission propagates to the final line cont(q f) = (a/b)(1/n) cont(n f) = q cont f.
fields.problem:
Title: Content of Scalar Multiple

Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Polynomial (Abstract Algebra)|polynomial]] with [[Definition:Rational Number|rational]] [[Definition:Polynomial Coefficient|coefficients]].

Let $\cont f$ denote the [[Definition:Content of Rational Polynomial|content]] of $f$.

Let $q \in \Q$ be a [[Definition:Rational Number|rational number]].

Then:

:$\cont {q f} = q \cont f$
fields.source_context:
0001 | Let $q = \dfrac a b$ with $a, b \in \Z$.
0002 | 
0003 | Let $\Z \sqbrk X$ denote the [[Definition:Ring of Polynomials|ring of polynomials]] over $\Z$.
0004 | 
0005 | Let $n \in \Z$ such that $n f \in \Z \sqbrk X$. 
0006 | 
0007 | Then we have:
0008 | :$b n \paren {q f} = a n f \in \Z \sqbrk X$
0009 | 
0010 | By the definition of [[Definition:Content of Rational Polynomial|content]], and using that $a \in \Z$:
0011 | :$\cont {b n q f} = a \cont {n f}$
0012 | 
0013 | By definition of [[Definition:Content of Rational Polynomial|content]]:
0014 | :$\cont {q f} = \dfrac 1 {b n} \cont {b n q f}$
0015 | 
0016 | Combining the above with the definition of $\cont f$:
0017 | :$\cont {q f} = \dfrac a b \dfrac 1 n \cont {n f} = q \cont f$
0018 | {{Qed}}
0019 | 
0020 | [[Category:Polynomial Theory]]
0021 | [[Category:Content of Polynomial]]
fields.witness: Take a=-1, b=n=2, q=-1/2 and f=X+1. Then g=nf=2X+2 and bnqf=-g. Both integer polynomials have normalized content 2, but a cont(g)=-2. The selected Lean theorem computes these contents and the scalar arithmetic, refuting cont(bnqf)=a cont(nf). This local identity needs |a|. Under the corresponding rational-content convention, the stated final identity likewise needs |q|; that rational-content statement is a mathematical consequence explained here, not part of the selected Lean theorem.

scope_metadata.formal_scope: Selected theorem computes integer Polynomial.content of g=2X+2 and -g and the chosen rational scalar arithmetic. Rational-content consequences in prose are not an additional selected Lean theorem.
scope_metadata.source_kind: Content-scaling claim with an unrestricted negative scalar.
scope_metadata.target_scope: The integral-scalar content step with a=-1,b=n=2,q=-1/2,f=X+1. Its failure depends on the sign of a, not independently on the sign of b.
